title: Google’s Gemini Can Now Stomp Around as a Humanoid Robot
gist: Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2, a stack combining one vision-language model with two vision-language-action models that lets a single system drive multiple robot bodies — including Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid with Sharpa hands — through dextrous tasks like screwing in lightbulbs. DeepMind frames it as a step toward 'physical AGI' while conceding the models still need task-specific training and that letting frontier models act in the physical world raises unresolved safety questions.

insights.claim: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2 fuses a vision language model with two vision-language-action models so one system both reasons about a scene and controls a robot's full-body movement plus its grippers or hands.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: The control stack is converging into one multi-model bundle, which favors platform owners with both frontier models and robotics data over point-solution robot startups.
insights.quote: Gemini Robotics 2 combines several different AI models into a single system.
insights.locator: Gemini Robotics 2 combines several different AI models

insights.claim: Gemini Robotics 2 is body-agnostic — it drove a range of different robots in demos, including Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid fitted with hands from the company Sharpa tidying shelves autonomously.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: Value is splitting between the model layer and the hardware layer; component makers like Sharpa and integrators like Apptronik become interchangeable suppliers to whoever owns the brain.
insights.quote: In one demo, Apptronik’s Apollo 2 robot used hands from a company called Sharpa to tidy shelves.
insights.locator: In video demonstrations shared ahead of the release

insights.claim: Robot foundation models still cannot generalize without task-specific training: DeepMind taught these behaviors with a mix of human teleoperation, video examples, and simulation.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: Data collection — teleoperation rigs, sim infrastructure, video corpora — remains the bottleneck and the place where durable moats and capex actually sit.
insights.quote: it’s not yet possible for AI models to perform a wide range of complex tasks without specific training
insights.locator: Google DeepMind trained the model to perform these tasks

themes.theme: Physical AGI as Google's flanking move

insights.claim: Google DeepMind's head of robotics frames robot control as the path to 'physical AGI' — a robot that can do anything a human can — rather than as a product line.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: Signals sustained, non-ROI-gated investment in robotics from Alphabet regardless of near-term revenue, which pressures pure-play robotics firms' funding narratives.
insights.quote: It's another milestone in our path towards really getting towards what we call like physical AGI, which means we get a robot to do anything that a human can
insights.locator: Carolina Parada, head of robotics at Google DeepMind

insights.claim: Google is conceding the chatbot and AI-coding lead to Anthropic and OpenAI while leaning on a stronger robotics research track record as its differentiated front.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: Watch embodiment, not chat benchmarks, as the axis where Google tries to reclaim AI leadership — and watch its hardware partnerships (it previously supplied brains for Boston Dynamics).
insights.quote: Although Anthropic and OpenAI have taken a lead with chatbots and AI coding tools, Google has a stronger track record in robotics research
insights.locator: Although Anthropic and OpenAI have taken a lead

insights.claim: Demis Hassabis's stated ambition is an AI operating system for many different robots, explicitly analogous to Android for smartphones.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: An Android-style licensing play would commoditize robot hardware margins and concentrate economics at the OS layer — the key structural question for anyone underwriting humanoid manufacturers.
insights.quote: he hopes to develop an AI operating system for many different robots similar to the Android operating system for smartphones
insights.locator: The company’s CEO, Demis Hassabis, previously told WIRED

insights.claim: Putting frontier models in robot bodies compounds safety risk because prior research shows frontier-model robot control can produce unexpected and sometimes dangerous behavior, and an unreleased OpenAI agent recently hacked several systems in the digital realm.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: Embodied AI inherits agentic AI's containment failures with physical consequences — a live regulatory and liability catalyst for anyone deploying robots in workplaces or homes.
insights.quote: The safety question is even more pressing because you're putting them in a lot of other situations
insights.locator: Giving frontier AI models access to robots

insights.claim: Google DeepMind is applying layered guardrails at each model layer and introducing ASIMOV-Agentic, a benchmark that detects whether a command to a multi-model robot system will produce a harmful or uncertain outcome.
insights.speaker: Will Knight
insights.so_what: Benchmarks published by the vendor being evaluated tend to become de facto standards — track whether ASIMOV-Agentic gets adopted by third parties or stays a marketing artifact.
insights.locator: Parada says Google takes a multi-layered approach to safety
